method: Optuna TPE (seed 42); trial 0 enqueued as the untuned defaults so the search can only improve on them
objective: Minimise mean CV log loss, 3-fold trip-grouped GroupKFold on a 60,000-GPS-point subsample of the 80 training trips (448,912 candidate rows). Log loss is used because the HMM consumes the probabilities as emissions.

comparison.metric: CV macro F1 (5-fold trip-grouped, all 80 train trips)
Fit time on all training data (s)

conclusion: The tuned model is marginally better on cross-validation (log loss 0.1564 to 0.1555, macro F1 0.8562 to 0.8566) and on student-test top-1 and macro F1 (+0.001 and +0.0006), with student-test log loss unchanged (0.1356 vs 0.1357). These differences are far below the fold-to-fold standard deviation (about 0.03 in log loss), so tuning did not meaningfully change accuracy: the defaults were already near the optimum for these six features. The tuned model is smaller (300 trees vs 500) and fits about 37% faster (20.6 s vs 32.8 s) with 19% faster inference.
compute_cost: 25 trials in about 12 minutes (729 s) on 4 CPU cores; the untuned and tuned comparison (two 5-fold CVs plus two full refits) took about 8 more minutes.
